figures.label: Figure 1
figures.caption: Model Lineage of the Qwen Series. We have pretrained the language models, namely Qwen, on massive datasets containing trillions of tokens. We then use SFT and RLHF to align Qwen to human preference and thus we have Qwen-Chat and specifically its improved version Qwen-Chat-RLHF. Additionally, we also develop specialized models for coding and mathematics, such as Code-Qwen, Code-Qwen-Chat, and Math-Qwen-Chat based on Qwen with similar techniques. Note that we previously released the multimodal LLM, Qwen-VL and Qwen-VL-Chat (Bai et al., 2023), which are also based on our Qwen base models.
figures.headline: Qwen base models are aligned into Qwen-Chat by finetuning and RLHF, and coding and math models are built on Qwen.

figures.label: Figure 2
figures.caption: Performance of GPT-4, GPT-3.5, the previous 13B SOTA, as well as Qwen-14B. We demonstrate the results on $12$ datasets covering multiple domains, including language understanding, knowledge, reasoning, etc. Qwen significantly outperforms the previous SOTA of similar model sizes, but still lag behind both GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.
figures.headline: Qwen-14B beats the previous 13B best model across 12 datasets but trails GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.

figures.label: Figure 3
figures.caption: Encoding compression rates of different models. We randomly selected $1$ million document corpora of each language to test and compare the encoding compression rates of different models (with XLM-R (Conneau et al., 2019), which supports $100$ languages, as the base value $1$, not shown in the figure). As can be seen, while ensuring the efficient decoding of Chinese, English, and code, Qwen also achieves a high compression rate for many other languages (such as th, he, ar, ko, vi, ja, tr, id, pl, ru, nl, pt, it, de, es, fr, etc.), equipping the model with strong scalability as well as high training and inference efficiency in these languages.
figures.headline: Qwen's tokenizer compresses text more efficiently than rival tokenizers in most languages, including Chinese, English and code.
citing_sentences: The performance of the Qwen tokenizer in terms of compression is depicted in Figure 3.

figures.label: Figure 4
figures.caption: Results of the human evaluation for chat models. We compare Qwen-7B (SFT), Qwen-14B (SFT), Qwen-14B (RLHF), as well as GPT-4 against GPT-3.5. Each bar segment represents the percentage of wins, ties, and losses, from bottom to top. On average, the RLHF model outperforms the SFT model. The dataset consists of 300 Chinese instructions.
figures.headline: On average, the RLHF version of Qwen-14B wins more human comparisons against GPT-3.5 than its SFT version.
citing_sentences: Figure 4 illustrates the win rates of the various models.

abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have revolutionized the field of artificial intelligence, enabling natural language processing tasks that were previously thought to be exclusive to humans. In this work, we introduce Qwen, the first installment of our large language model series. Qwen is a comprehensive language model series that encompasses distinct models with varying parameter counts. It includes Qwen, the base pretrained language models, and Qwen-Chat, the chat models finetuned with human alignment techniques. The base language models consistently demonstrate superior performance across a multitude of downstream tasks, and the chat models, particularly those trained using Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF), are highly competitive. The chat models possess advanced tool-use and planning capabilities for creating agent applications, showcasing impressive performance even when compared to bigger models on complex tasks like utilizing a code interpreter. Furthermore, we have developed coding-specialized models, Code-Qwen and Code-Qwen-Chat, as well as mathematics-focused models, Math-Qwen-Chat, which are built upon base language models. These models demonstrate significantly improved performance in comparison with open-source models, and slightly fall behind the proprietary models.

sections.body:
The section introduces Qwen, a model series with base models, chat models finetuned with supervised finetuning and RLHF, and specialized coding and math models.

- The base Qwen models are trained on up to 3 trillion tokens of text and code.
- Qwen-Chat models trained with RLHF are reported as highly competitive, but still fall behind GPT-4 on the authors' own benchmark.
- Code-Qwen is evaluated on HumanEval, MBPP and HumanEvalPack.
- Math-Qwen-Chat 7B and 14B outperform open-source models of the same size and approach GPT-3.5 on GSM8K and MATH.
- The 14B and 7B base and chat models are released as open-source. The multimodal Qwen-VL models were released earlier.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Qwen is a series of base, chat, coding and math language models, with the 14B and 7B base and chat models released openly.

sections.body: The data pipeline uses public web pages, encyclopedias, books and code, with exact and MinHash/LSH fuzzy deduplication, rule-based and model-based filtering, and removal of instruction samples with 13-gram overlap against test sets. The tokenizer starts from `cl100k_base` and grows to a vocabulary of about 152K. The architecture is a modified LLaMA-style Transformer with untied embeddings, RoPE, SwiGLU and RMSNorm. Table 1 lists 1.8B, 7B and 14B models trained on 2.2T, 2.4T and 3.0T tokens. In Table 2, Qwen-14B outperforms LLaMA2-70B on 3 tasks. In Table 3, arXiv perplexity for Qwen-7B is 2645.09 at 16384 tokens without the extension techniques and 4.32 with dynamic NTK, LogN scaling and window attention.
sections.heading: Pretraining
sections.headline: Qwen base models trained on up to 3 trillion tokens are compared with open-source baselines on 7 benchmarks, with extended-context perplexity reported.

sections.body: Supervised finetuning uses ChatML-formatted, human-style conversations with safety-related annotation, trained with next-token loss, sequence length 2048, batch size 128 and 4000 steps. The reward model starts from Qwen with a pooling layer. In Table 4, the Qwen Helpful-online test accuracy is 61.62 for the PMP model and 69.71 for the reward model. Reinforcement learning uses PPO with four models and a KL coefficient of 0.04. Table 5 reports Qwen-14B-Chat outperforming all other models except ChatGPT and Llama 2-Chat-70B. Tool-use accuracy rises with model size but shows little gain beyond a certain size, and the authors call their benchmark preliminary and possibly easy. Figure 4 human evaluation uses 300 Chinese instructions.
sections.heading: Alignment
sections.headline: Chat models are aligned by supervised finetuning and RLHF, with Qwen-14B-Chat trailing only ChatGPT and Llama 2-Chat-70B on the reported benchmarks.

sections.body:
Code-Qwen continues pretraining the Qwen base models on around 90 billion code tokens, not on code alone, with context length up to 8192 and a learning rate of 6.0 × 10^-5 for 14B and 3.0 × 10^-5 for 7B. Code-Qwen-Chat is produced by a multi-stage SFT strategy.

- Table 10: Code-Qwen-Chat 14B scores 66.4 on HumanEval and 52.4 on MBPP. Code-Qwen 14B scores 45.1 and 51.4.
- Table 11: Code-Qwen-Chat 14B averages 51.9 across HumanEvalPack programming languages, against 78.3 for GPT-4.

The authors state that these models fall behind GPT-4 overall and that the current evaluations are insufficient to show their full strengths and weaknesses.
sections.heading: Code-Qwen: Specialized Model for Coding
sections.headline: Code-Qwen continues pretraining Qwen on about 90 billion code tokens, reaching 66.4 pass@1 on HumanEval for the 14B chat model.

sections.body: Math-Qwen-Chat is built on the Qwen pretrained models and trained with math SFT on an augmented math instruction dataset, which yields the chat model directly. Training uses sequence length 1024, masks system and user inputs from the loss, and a peak learning rate of $2\times 10^{-5}$. Evaluation uses greedy decoding on GSM8K, MATH, Math401 and Math23K. In Table 12, Math-Qwen-Chat 7B scores 62.5 on GSM8K and 17.2 on MATH, and 14B scores 69.8 and 24.2, versus 50.3 and 6.8 for Qwen-Chat 7B. The text says Math-Qwen-7B-Chat outperforms Minerva-8B on MATH, and that Math-Qwen-14B-Chat is described as chasing Minerva-62B and GPT-3.5 on GSM8K and MATH.
sections.heading: Math-Qwen: Specialized Model for Mathematics Reasoning
sections.headline: Math-Qwen-Chat 14B scores 69.8 on grade-school math problems and 24.2 on competition math, against 60.1 and 18.4 for Qwen-Chat 14B.

sections.body: Related work traces Transformer-based pretraining, with model sizes growing from 100 million to over 10 billion parameters and GPT-3 described as 10 times larger than T5. It covers open-source models such as LLaMA and Llama 2, and alignment methods including SFT, RLHF, LoRA, Q-LoRA, RRHF, DPO and PRO. It discusses tool-use agents such as ReAct, code models such as Codex and Code LLaMA, and math reasoning methods such as chain-of-thought prompting. The authors state that more evidence is needed on how RLHF improves the intelligence of LLMs and what drawbacks it may have.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Related work covers large model scaling, open-source chat models, tool-use agents, code models and math reasoning methods.

sections.body: The conclusion summarizes the Qwen series as 14B, 7B and 1.8B parameter models, pretrained on trillions of tokens and finetuned with SFT and RLHF. It also lists Code-Qwen, Code-Qwen-Chat and Math-Qwen-Chat as domain-specific models. The authors state that the results show the series is competitive with existing open-source models and matches the performance of some proprietary models on comprehensive benchmarks and human evaluation. They say open access is intended to foster collaboration and innovation, and they describe the release as a major milestone in their development of large language models.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: Qwen's report concludes that its models are competitive with open-source models and match some proprietary models on benchmarks and human evaluation.

sections.body:
The appendix gives the ChatML-style data format, which uses the special tokens `im_start` and `im_end` that do not appear in pretraining, and contrasts it with the human-assistant format.

- Table 13 (MMLU): Qwen 14B averages 66.3 with five-shot accuracy.
- Table 14 (C-Eval): Qwen 14B averages 72.1.
- Table 15: CMMLU, AGIEval, ARC-e and ARC-c.
- Table 16: BoolQ, CommonsenseQA, NaturalQuestions and LAMBADA.
- Table 17: HellaSwag, PIQA, SIQA and OCNLI.

The last part describes human evaluation cases in Chinese, with Elo ratings for all models.
sections.heading: Appendix
sections.headline: The appendix lists the chat data format, automatic evaluation tables for examination, knowledge and reasoning benchmarks, and human evaluation cases.
